chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-A'azz al-Nakhhas, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I treat the animals, so sometimes I go out at night and they have urinated or excreted, so one of them strikes it with its foot or its hand, so it splashes upon my clothes. So I wake up in the morning and I see its traces in it.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon you.'

key_terms.الدَّوَابَّ: Animals (specifically beasts of burden or livestock)
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ شَيْءٌ: There is nothing upon you (no obligation to remove it)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on animal urine splashing on clothes during night work?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) grants a concession to those who work with animals, ruling that incidental splashes of urine or excrement do not invalidate ritual purity. This establishes the principle of *al-‘urf* (customary practice) and ease in jurisprudence, acknowledging that minor, unavoidable impurities for specific professions are excused, thereby simplifying the performance of prayer for the working class.
